correctness.rationale: Independently recovered the joint order and tree law: with seen set S, current x and u=n−|S|, a specified next new label y with predecessor z∈S has probability (1+u·1[z=x])/(nu). The immediate jump contributes 1/n only for z=x; summing strings of one or more old draws ending at z contributes 1/(nu). Multiplication yields the stated order weights times a common factor, with the first root discovery contributing a common numerator n. For the permutation expansion, remove the ancestor-closed prefix, write a=τ_i and b=τ_{i+1}. In a valid suffix input the first scanned symbol has b as its first available ancestor in the forest without a. Reinserting a later than first prepends a to that first chain exactly when p(b)=a; otherwise b would precede a. Reinserting a first always works since a has no un-emitted ancestor. Erasing a preserves the shorter expansion, so this induction exhausts the distinct input permutations, giving exactly the displayed product. The latest scanned leaf is the latest output: leaves cannot be emitted earlier, and every internal vertex precedes an output descendant leaf. Uniform permutations assign each leaf probability 1/|Λ(T)|. This also covers k=1, a unique leaf, and suppression of holding steps.
residual_risks: The mass comparison for the last discovery is specific to uniform complete-graph transitions and does not extend in this proof to arbitrary edge weights or intermediate discovery ranks.
